title: audit-afd-p2p-exchanges
summary: Audit CUDA P2pNccl Attention/FFN rank namespaces and per-stage, per-peer hidden-state ownership when uneven worker counts or a mismatched return slice make an AFD exchange ambiguous.

skill_metadata.name: audit-afd-p2p-exchanges
skill_metadata.description: Audit CUDA P2pNccl Attention/FFN rank namespaces and per-stage, per-peer hidden-state ownership when uneven worker counts or a mismatched return slice make an AFD exchange ambiguous.

applicability.scope: Source-based CUDA P2pNccl rank/payload audit; selected eager dense-FFN path with compute_gate_on_attention=false. Repository identity afd_plugin; runtime/backend compatibility unverified.
applicability.prerequisites: Access to the pinned source ledger and caller-level evidence for the selected eager dense FFN path with Attention-side gating disabled; any proposed cross-stream reuse needs an established communicator completion contract.
applicability.input_contract: Plugin and dependency revisions, connector and role, A/F worker counts, DP/PCP/TP coordinates, worker/device ranks, subgroup roster, stage, per-peer token counts, payload shape/dtype/device, transfer context and returned slices.
applicability.produced_artifact: A bounded rank-namespace and per-peer payload ownership ledger, the earliest evidenced mismatch or missing edge, and a proposed verification plan.
applicability.failure_modes: Inferring data peers from control senders, accepting equal total row counts despite a peer permutation, or treating an even-split fallback or Python return as proof of ownership/completion can produce a wrong exchange diagnosis.
applicability.refusal_point: Stop on A < F, invalid role ranks, duplicate/missing assignments or an unresolved rank namespace; return the conflicting callers and ledger entries without inventing ranks or attributing the fault to networking.

limitations: Source-derived candidate; native exchange, model quality, backend compatibility, performance and agent efficacy not_run.
Selected Python readset is Apache-2.0; the retained MIT notice concerns excluded NPU async CAM implementation and adapted bindings.
No qualification of graph/DBO, remote-expert MoE, multi-host transport, complete token-count projection or underlying communicator completion semantics.
recommendations: Record role, world and subgroup-local ranks separately; reconstruct the actual subgroup roster before interpreting send/receive peers.
Track distinct row identities and stage-specific peer lengths through concatenation and splitting; use same-total swapped lengths as a countercheck.
Establish the last communicator/stream completion obligation before reusing or releasing a receive buffer.
